---
title: "Course Overview"
---

## Purpose

The St Helena Public Health Data Skills Programme builds practical capability in analysing and communicating public health data.

The programme is designed for small teams working in real-world health systems with limited resources.

## Design Principles

The programme emphasises:

- practical workflows
- reproducible analysis
- responsible handling of health data
- clear communication of evidence

Participants learn to move from:

raw data → cleaned datasets → analysis → safe outputs → policy-relevant communication.

## Data Protection and Confidentiality

A core component of the programme is the safe handling of individual-level health data.

Key topics include:

- confidentiality of patient data
- principles of GDPR and responsible data governance
- anonymisation and de-identification
- aggregation and disclosure control
- suppression of small numbers
- safe public reporting

## Learning Structure

Each module contains:

- short conceptual explanations
- worked examples (primarily in **Stata**)
- optional “try-it-yourself” exercises
- practical tasks based on real public health workflows
